name: Marrying An Unsaved Person
overview: Scripture reveals that marriage is a divinely ordained union designed for companionship and unity, as God created a suitable helper for man and established that a man shall leave his parents and cleave to his wife, becoming one flesh (Genesis 2:18, 2:24). The New Testament emphasizes the sanctity and permanence of marriage, warning against divorce and remarriage except in the case of fornication, as such actions lead to adultery (Matthew 5:32; Mark 10:11). Additionally, husbands are called to love their wives sacrificially, as Christ loved the church (Ephesians 5:25), highlighting the spiritual significance and responsibility within marriage. The law's authority over a person while alive (Romans 7:1) further underscores the binding nature of the marriage covenant, implying that marrying an unsaved person must be considered carefully in light of these biblical principles.
